title: Unsupervised Machine Learning for Atomic-Resolution S(TEM) Image Analysis and Management
content: High-resolution imaging has become an essential tool for studying materials in detail at the atomic level. Major imaging techniques include advanced microscopy methods such as (scanning) transmission electron microscopy (S)TEM. With the continuous development of high-resolution imaging technologies and their widespread application across various scientific disciplines, including condensed matter physics, materials engineering, and biology, a vast amount of microscopy data is generated daily [1, 2]. Consequently, there is an urgent need to efficiently analyze and manage this extensive data to facilitate the discovery of new materials and to understand the structural features that influence material properties.
